lots.guide_summary: Only one close entry survives: the Nye plaster coat-and-hat figure that PASSED in 2017 at an estimate of US$300 to 500 (A$431 to 718 at 1.4358). No same-item SOLD or ASKING. Category evidence: Gowans SOLD hammers for ordinary full-size mannequins $40 to $140 and display figures $80 to $110 (12 months); overseas dealer ASKING A$359 to A$3,590 for display mannequins and stylised figures, which are optimistic and mostly older or named-maker pieces. Rates 1 USD = 1.4358 AUD, 1 EUR = 1.6130 AUD, 1 GBP = 1.9139 AUD (open.er-api.com, read 19 Oct 2026 by the researcher).
lots.working: No same-item or close SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For scale only (not a bid): local Gowans hammers for full-size mannequins sit at $40 to $140, so at $100 hammer the all-in cost would be $122. The single close comparable did not sell even at a US$300 low estimate.
lots.confidence_reason: Maker unknown, cuff inscription illegible at the supplied resolution (450 x 600 photos), date and Myer provenance unverified, and the only close entry is an unsold 2017 US estimate.
lots.key_photo_findings: Four photos re-checked. Faint scratched or incised marks on the left forearm/cuff stay illegible when cropped and enlarged 3x (photos are only 450 x 600). No label or stamp visible. Smooth faceted cast surface with a few small dark specks and light scuffs; feet sit on a separate clipped-corner glass plate with a small metal heel fixing. Hat brim and nose ridge intact as far as visible. No view of the back or the underside.
lots.condition: Appears sound from the front; minor surface marks and specks. Back, underside and base edges not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the writing on the left cuff (a signature, maker or date)? Is there any maker's stamp under the feet or on the back? What is it made of (plaster, resin or fibreglass) and how heavy is it? Any chips, cracks or repairs on the back, hat brim or nose? Is the glass base chipped, and does the Myer provenance come with any paperwork?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped as not the same kind of item (garden or decor statuary, not display figures): Gowans 442565 kangaroo figure $600, 419494 gargoyle $575 (and the 395071 gargoyle $480 mentioned in its note), 407549 lady statue $287, 439821 concrete lady statue $230, 441260 plaster statue $200. Dropped Lawsons 'Deco shop mannequin display in painted plaster' A$1,200: snippet only, no date, 1930s three-head display, a different class of object. Nye lot moved from category guide to close (same design concept) but stays UNSOLD. Lot 95 foreign prices recalculated at 1 USD = 1.4358 for consistency.

lots.guide_summary: Close entries: SOLD 5 (A$165 in 2023 for a worn group, then A$290, A$355, A$609 and A$1,160 in the last 24 months, all overseas hammer, premium extra), UNSOLD 1 (A$161 last bid for a worm-eaten hanging putto), ASKING 1 (A$1,436 dealer ask for a Baroque Revival floating putto). Local Tasmanian carved-figure hammers ran $40 to $340 but no carved putto has sold at Gowans in the last year. Rates 1 USD = 1.4358 AUD, 1 EUR = 1.6130 AUD, 1 GBP = 1.9139 AUD (open.er-api.com, read 19 Oct 2026 by the researcher). Auctionet amounts are its own USD display of the house currency.
lots.working: Close SOLD in the last 24 months, damaged decorative putti: A$290 (US$202, Stockholms Auktionsverk, 17 Jul 2026, painted 57 cm, cracks and missing parts), A$355 (US$247, Lawrences, 27 Dec 2024, natural limewood 25 cm), A$609 (US$424, gilded, 20 Dec 2025), A$1,160 (US$808, 35-bid polychrome outlier). Keep: lowest = A$290 / 1.22 = 237.7, round down to $235 hammer ($286.70 all-in). Flip: likely resale taken conservatively as A$355 (the natural-finish result; the higher ones are gilded, polychrome or contested), resold through a local auction room at about 15% seller's commission with $0 postage (local pickup) = A$301.75 net; / 2.44 = 123.7, round down to $120 hammer. Caution: all close SOLD evidence is overseas (UK and Sweden); no Tasmanian putto sale was found, so local resale may fall short.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification of type and four close SOLD pages opened, but no maker's mark, age unproven, size not stated, and no same-item Australian sale.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos re-checked. Well-carved curly-haired putto with expressive face; glossy shellac or varnish. Visible hairline crack running across the shoulder into the upper arm (photo 3) and a crack across the back of the raised arm (photo 2). Round wooden plug over an old fixing hole and two small pin holes in the back. The ring is a separate turned piece bound with rawhide, which looks like a repair or later fitting. A paper tag hangs from the ring. No marks seen.
lots.condition: Hairline cracks at the shoulder and upper arm, old fixing plug, ring possibly a later or repaired part. Otherwise surface looks good with no obvious losses to fingers or toes in the photos.
lots.question_for_armitage: What is the full length (the title is cut off at 'L-4...')? Is the shoulder crack stable or does the arm move? Is the ring original or a replacement, and how is it attached to the hand? Any worm holes, missing fingers or toes? Any marks or old labels on the back?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Pamono 'Winged putto playing the wind instrument' (https://www.pamono.eu/winged-putto-playing-the-wind-instrument-carved-in-wood-early-1900s): researcher claimed EUR 1,650 but the page I opened shows EUR 200 (reduced from EUR 250), so the claimed price is wrong; it is also only 32 cm. All 13 Auctionet entries re-opened and the embedded state, bid amount and end date matched the researcher. Gowans and Lion and Unicorn entries re-checked and correct. Snippet-only Bonhams and TimeLine kept as leads only.

lots.confidence_reason: Label read clearly, but no verified SOLD price for a named Lincoln Bennett hat; size and condition of the nap unknown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos re-checked. Tip label clearly reads 'Lincoln Bennett & Co Hatters Piccadilly London' with the royal arms in red and gold. The nap in photo 2 is long and glossy, consistent with silk plush rather than felt; low crown with curled brim and ribbon band, looks like a riding or hunting topper. Some brown spotting (foxing) on the tip label and lining. No size marking visible. Gloves: several pairs of leather and string-backed driving gloves, some still in packets.
lots.condition: Hat looks clean with nap intact in the photo; light spotting to the lining. Sweatband and size not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: What size is the hat (inside circumference or size stamp on the sweatband)? Is it silk plush, and is the nap rubbed or bald anywhere? Is the leather sweatband intact? Any maker or retailer marks on the gloves?
